hushgram.title: v0.0.15
hushgram.body:
## [0.0.15](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushGram/compare/v0.0.14...v0.0.15) (2026-10-22)

### Features

* **Instagram:** New switch under Downloads, `Add the source to saved photos`, off to start. A saved JPEG photo carries the account that posted it, the post date and the post's link in its EXIF details. The picture doesn't change.
* **Instagram - Download any reel:** Reels on the Reels tab get Details and Copy caption in their menu now, the same as feed posts. (#282)

### Bug Fixes

* **Instagram - Hide Follow on feed posts:** The Subscribe button next to a creator's name on feed posts goes too now. On Reels it goes with Clean up Reels' follow switch. A creator's own profile keeps its button. (#248)
* **Instagram - Clean up Reels:** With `Keep clear mode on`, a long reel in clear mode no longer keeps its seek bar along the bottom. The bar comes back once you leave clear mode. (#277)
* **Instagram - Clean up Reels:** With `Keep clear mode on`, the buttons, author row and top bar could pop back up a few swipes in while a reel was still in clear mode. They stay hidden now, and come back when clear mode ends. Reported in #233.
* **Instagram - Hide the Explore grid:** Turning on `Hide suggested accounts in search` took your recent searches away too. Now it hides only the Suggested for you accounts. (#272)
* **Instagram - Turn off HDR brightness boosts:** On Instagram's armeabi-v7a builds (for 32-bit phones) the switch now turns off SDR super white and Ultra HDR always on too. Before, only the arm64 build had those two options turned off. (#85)
* **Instagram - HushGram settings:** The settings shortcut on the app icon no longer shows a second of Reels (or whatever tab Instagram opens on) before the settings come up. The screen stays black until they're drawn. (#55)
* **Instagram - Download any video:** Saved reels play with sound in more apps. Some reels carry only xHE-AAC sound, which many players turn silent. When the post also has a plain video file, the save keeps the best picture and takes that file's sound. Refs #242.
* **Instagram - Glass tab bar:** With the pill floating, a reel stops above the pill again, as in 0.0.13, so there's no wide black band over the video. The seek bar stays clear of the pill and the gesture handle. (#280)
* **Instagram - Glass tab bar:** A reel keeps one size while comments, the keyboard and a paused reel's controls come and go, and the glass doesn't draw the reel's video into its blur anymore. Both made a playing reel resize. (#222)
* **Instagram - Glass tab bar:** If the blur ever drops to the plain dark tint while you scroll, it comes back by itself a moment later. Before, it stayed that way until Instagram restarted. (#262)
* **Instagram - Start Home on Following:** Tapping Back to home at the end of your Following feed closed Instagram. Now it switches Home to For you, like picking it from the top menu. With `Only accounts you follow` on, Home just stays on Following.
* **Instagram - Pure black dark mode:** Stories are black around the edges too. The thin strip above a story and the bar behind its reply field kept Instagram's dark gray before. The story itself keeps its colors. (#279)

### Improvements

* **Instagram:** HushGram now patches Instagram 452.1.0.53.64 instead of 452.0.0.48.64. Get APKMirror's (arm64-v8a) (480-640dpi) (Android 9.0+) variant, build 385811006. The armeabi-v7a build (385811005) patches too, and so do the x86 and x86_64 builds (385811007 and 385811008), which Instagram is shipping again.
* **Instagram:** HushGram now builds on Morphe patcher 2.0.0, so update Morphe Manager to 2.0.0 or newer before patching. On a computer, use morphe-desktop 1.19.0 or newer. Patching with every patch on takes about 40% less time there. (#60)
* **Instagram - Find the reel you came from:** Trial reels (shown to people who don't follow the creator) aren't on the creator's profile, so the search could only give up. Tapping the creator of one now shows a short note and skips the search. Reported in #225.
* **Instagram - Download any video:** Skip what's already saved reads its history file in small, fixed amounts now. A damaged file can't slow a save down, and it gets written out fresh at the next save, so newer saves aren't lost behind the damage. (#150)
* **Instagram - Turn off double tap to like:** Patching takes about 4% less time with every patch on. The patch reads code only in the places its targets can be, instead of every method in the app. The patched app comes out the same. Refs #173.
* **Instagram - View stories anonymously:** Patching with every patch on takes about 3% less time and 5% less processor work. Its checks for other callers now read only the classes that can hold one. The patched app doesn't change. Refs #173.
* **Instagram:** HushGram launch screen and Emoji style now ask the patcher's index where their code is, instead of reading every method. With every patch on, that's about 3% less processor work. Same patched app as before. Refs #173.
* **Instagram:** Patches that find their code by a piece of text, or by Instagram's internal labels, now look it up directly instead of checking every string. Patching is about 2% quicker. The patched app is the same. Refs #173.
* **Tooling:** `scripts/native-runner.ps1` runs checks inside the installed patched Instagram on an offline emulator, as a throwaway signed-out Android user. Each verdict names the exact APK it ran on. Two controls (build identity, a missing hook) must hold before feature checks count.
* **Tooling:** The native runner's first feature checks cover Hide your active status. They build Instagram's own presence requests without sending them, and only Active may turn Idle, only while the switch is on and HushGram isn't paused.
* **Tooling:** The native runner checks View DM photos and videos anonymously on Instagram's receipt handler. Switched on, the handler finishes a stand-in receipt on the phone without building its request. Voice receipts, a paused HushGram and the switch off stay Instagram's.
* **Tooling:** Nothing goes public until the whole app has been walked with that exact bundle on a release phone or an emulator. `publish-release.ps1` stops before GitHub without a full, crash-free walk of that bundle.
* **Tooling:** `scripts/find-release-for-identity.ps1` reads the `hg1:` build identity from a diagnostics report and names the release it came from, or says the build isn't one of ours, so a repackaged fork shows up before anyone digs in.

### Validation

Validation: 5910 runtime tests passed locally. All 2051 patch tests passed too.

repos.body:
## [0.0.15](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushGram/compare/v0.0.14...v0.0.15) (2026-10-22)

### Features

* **Instagram:** New switch under Downloads, `Add the source to saved photos`, off to start. A saved JPEG photo carries the account that posted it, the post date and the post's link in its EXIF details. The picture doesn't change.
* **Instagram - Download any reel:** Reels on the Reels tab get Details and Copy caption in their menu now, the same as feed posts. (#282)

### Bug Fixes

* **Instagram - Hide Follow on feed posts:** The Subscribe button next to a creator's name on feed posts goes too now. On Reels it goes with Clean up Reels' follow switch. A creator's own profile keeps its button. (#248)
* **Instagram - Clean up Reels:** With `Keep clear mode on`, a long reel in clear mode no longer keeps its seek bar along the bottom. The bar comes back once you leave clear mode. (#277)
* **Instagram - Clean up Reels:** With `Keep clear mode on`, the buttons, author row and top bar could pop back up a few swipes in while a reel was still in clear mode. They stay hidden now, and come back when clear mode ends. Reported in #233.
* **Instagram - Hide the Explore grid:** Turning on `Hide suggested accounts in search` took your recent searches away too. Now it hides only the Suggested for you accounts. (#272)
* **Instagram - Turn off HDR brightness boosts:** On Instagram's armeabi-v7a builds (for 32-bit phones) the switch now turns off SDR super white and Ultra HDR always on too. Before, only the arm64 build had those two options turned off. (#85)
* **Instagram - HushGram settings:** The settings shortcut on the app icon no longer shows a second of Reels (or whatever tab Instagram opens on) before the settings come up. The screen stays black until they're drawn. (#55)
* **Instagram - Download any video:** Saved reels play with sound in more apps. Some reels carry only xHE-AAC sound, which many players turn silent. When the post also has a plain video file, the save keeps the best picture and takes that file's sound. Refs #242.
* **Instagram - Glass tab bar:** With the pill floating, a reel stops above the pill again, as in 0.0.13, so there's no wide black band over the video. The seek bar stays clear of the pill and the gesture handle. (#280)
* **Instagram - Glass tab bar:** A reel keeps one size while comments, the keyboard and a paused reel's controls come and go, and the glass doesn't draw the reel's video into its blur anymore. Both made a playing reel resize. (#222)
* **Instagram - Glass tab bar:** If the blur ever drops to the plain dark tint while you scroll, it comes back by itself a moment later. Before, it stayed that way until Instagram restarted. (#262)
* **Instagram - Start Home on Following:** Tapping Back to home at the end of your Following feed closed Instagram. Now it switches Home to For you, like picking it from the top menu. With `Only accounts you follow` on, Home just stays on Following.
* **Instagram - Pure black dark mode:** Stories are black around the edges too. The thin strip above a story and the bar behind its reply field kept Instagram's dark gray before. The story itself keeps its colors. (#279)

### Improvements

* **Instagram:** HushGram now patches Instagram 452.1.0.53.64 instead of 452.0.0.48.64. Get APKMirror's (arm64-v8a) (480-640dpi) (Android 9.0+) variant, build 385811006. The armeabi-v7a build (385811005) patches too, and so do the x86 and x86_64 builds (385811007 and 385811008), which Instagram is shipping again.
* **Instagram:** HushGram now builds on Morphe patcher 2.0.0, so update Morphe Manager to 2.0.0 or newer before patching. On a computer, use morphe-desktop 1.19.0 or newer. Patching with every patch on takes about 40% less time there. (#60)
* **Instagram - Find the reel you came from:** Trial reels (shown to people who don't follow the creator) aren't on the creator's profile, so the search could only give up. Tapping the creator of one now shows a short note and skips the search. Reported in #225.
* **Instagram - Download any video:** Skip what's already saved reads its history file in small, fixed amounts now. A damaged file can't slow a save down, and it gets written out fresh at the next save, so newer saves aren't lost behind the damage. (#150)
* **Instagram - Turn off double tap to like:** Patching takes about 4% less time with every patch on. The patch reads code only in the places its targets can be, instead of every method in the app. The patched app comes out the same. Refs #173.
* **Instagram - View stories anonymously:** Patching with every patch on takes about 3% less time and 5% less processor work. Its checks for other callers now read only the classes that can hold one. The patched app doesn't change. Refs #173.
* **Instagram:** HushGram launch screen and Emoji style now ask the patcher's index where their code is, instead of reading every method. With every patch on, that's about 3% less processor work. Same patched app as before. Refs #173.
* **Instagram:** Patches that find their code by a piece of text, or by Instagram's internal labels, now look it up directly instead of checking every string. Patching is about 2% quicker. The patched app is the same. Refs #173.
* **Tooling:** `scripts/native-runner.ps1` runs checks inside the installed patched Instagram on an offline emulator, as a throwaway signed-out Android user. Each verdict names the exact APK it ran on. Two controls (build identity, a missing hook) must hold before feature checks count.
* **Tooling:** The native runner's first feature checks cover Hide your active status. They build Instagram's own presence requests without sending them, and only Active may turn Idle, only while the switch is on and HushGram isn't paused.
* **Tooling:** The native runner checks View DM photos and videos anonymously on Instagram's receipt handler. Switched on, the handler finishes a stand-in receipt on the phone without building its request. Voice receipts, a paused HushGram and the switch off stay Instagram's.
* **Tooling:** Nothing goes public until the whole app has been walked with that exact bundle on a release phone or an emulator. `publish-release.ps1` stops before GitHub without a full, crash-free walk of that bundle.
* **Tooling:** `scripts/find-release-for-identity.ps1` reads the `hg1:` build identity from a diagnostics report and names the release it came from, or says the build isn't one of ours, so a repackaged fork shows up before anyone digs in.

### Validation

Validation: 5910 runtime tests passed locally. All 2051 patch tests passed too.

hushpinterest.title: v0.0.12
hushpinterest.body:
HushPinterest 0.0.12 has 32 patches for Pinterest 14.41.0. It's built on Morphe patcher 1.15.1, so it needs Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer. This one moves to Pinterest's newest version and adds a lot of new switches, every one of them off until you turn it on. Filter feed can hide video pins and pins with words you mute. Keep Home feed stops Home from reloading on its own when you come back to it, and Show posted date puts the day a pin went up under its title. Download pins can copy or share the picture itself now, and its rows show in the full-screen pin menu too. Downloads also stopped settling for the smaller copy now and then.

It's a new Pinterest version. So far APKMirror only has 14.41.0 as an arm64 bundle (`.apkm`) for Android 12L or newer, and Manager merges it before patching. Patch it with the same signing key you used before and install it over your current HushPinterest, and your settings stay as they are. On a phone older than Android 12L, keep 0.0.11 and Pinterest 14.40.0 for now.

## What's new

- The patches now target Pinterest 14.41.0, the newest stable release. 14.40.0 is no longer supported. So far APKMirror has 14.41.0 only as an arm64 bundle (`.apkm`) for Android 12L or newer, and Manager merges it before patching.
- Download pin now shows in the full-screen pin menu some accounts get from the three dots on a pin, along with the other Hush rows, and Pinterest's own Download row in that menu gives way to it. Before, only the smaller pop-up menu had them.
- Download pins has a new switch, Copy image, that starts off. It adds a Copy image row under Download pin, in the small pin menu and in the full-screen one, and puts the full-size picture on the clipboard so you can paste it into a chat or a notes app. Video pins don't get the row. If the picture is too big, isn't really an image, or takes too long, you're told so and your clipboard stays as it was. (#11)
- Download pins also has Share image, another switch that starts off. Its row sits under Copy image and opens Android's share menu with the full-size picture itself rather than a link, so the app you pick gets the image. Video pins don't get it, and if the picture can't be fetched you get a short note instead of the share menu. (#11)
- Long-press download has three new switches on the Pin actions page: Hide Save, Hide Send and Hide Search image in the long-press menu. Each takes that one Pinterest button out of the round menu you get by holding a pin in a grid, and the pin itself still saves, shares and searches as before. They work with Download off too. If everything would be hidden and Download is off, the menu stays Pinterest's own rather than opening empty. All three start off. (#11)
- Black comments now covers the strip under the status bar too. On 14.41.0 the comments fill the whole screen, and that strip stayed dark gray above the black list on photo and video pins alike.
- Downloads no longer save the smaller copy now and then when the original is there. Finding the original asks Pinterest's media server a few quick questions, and one asked just as both lookup helpers were wrapping up the last was turned away, so the download settled for the size the feed showed. It now waits a moment for a helper to come free.
- Copy media link no longer overwrites something you copied after it. When a pin shows only a smaller size, the link to that size goes on the clipboard right away, and it becomes the original's link once Pinterest's media server answers, but only if the clipboard still holds that copy. Before, nothing was copied until the answer came, and a slow answer could replace whatever you'd copied in the meantime.
- Save list no longer hangs when the app holding the picked file stops answering. Each save gets 30 seconds in all, then you're told to check the file, and a late answer from that app doesn't add another message or remove anything. While that app is still busy, a new list says to try later instead of opening a picker. Everything that talks to the file's app now runs on its own helper, never on the screen's thread, including the clean-up after a list that couldn't be written while HushPinterest was paused.
- A list that isn't written no longer deletes an empty file you picked to write over. Only an empty file made since the picker opened gets removed. Any other file is left where it is, and you're told so.
- Save list leaves out a source link that hides a session code behind an encoded `;` (`%3B`, that encoded again, or a longer spelling some servers still read as `;`), the way it already left out a plain `;jsessionid=`. The pin's ID, title and Pinterest link still go in. Ordinary encoded spaces and accented letters stay exactly as given.
- Queue selected and Queue pins stay off until something chosen can actually be saved. A pin with no picture address, or a video Pinterest only streams, doesn't turn them on anymore, though Save list still takes those pins. A mix still queues what it can and counts the rest as unsupported.
- Morphe Manager lists every change of the release your Pinterest was patched with, not just a short summary. For that one release Manager shows the patch bundle's description instead of this changelog, and the description was one paragraph while every older release listed its changes. It now goes on with the release's changes after the summary, starting with this one.
- Hide comments has a second switch, Hide suggested replies, for the row of ready-made replies like "Yum!" and "Came out great!" next to the comment box. You can still write your own comment. It starts off, and the two switches don't turn each other on. (#14)
- Hide AI-labeled pins has a second switch, Hide pins that say they're AI, for AI pins Pinterest doesn't label. It takes a pin whose title or description says something like "AI art", "AI generated", #aiart, "made with AI", Midjourney, Stable Diffusion or PixAI, and pins from sites that only host AI images, like pixai.art and Civitai. It goes by the pin's own words, so a pin that just says "AI" stays, and names like Ai Weiwei or the Portuguese "aí" are left alone. Boards named that way stay too. It starts off, and diagnostics count these pins apart from the labeled ones.
- Hide closeup buttons has a third switch, Hide Search image label on pins. Pinterest puts a "Search image" label on the lens button for your first two pins each day, and with this on the lens shows without it, the way it looks from the third pin on. Tapping the lens still searches. It starts off and sits under Hide lens button on the Interface page. (#13)
- New Filter feed patch, with a Hide video pins switch on the Feed page. It takes pins that play a video out of your home feed, search, related pins and boards, idea pins with video included. Photos and GIFs stay. It starts off.
- Filter feed also has Muted words, a row on the Feed page where you type words and phrases you don't want to see. A pin whose title or description has one of them leaves the same lists. Capitals don't matter and only whole words count, so "cake" takes out "Wedding Cake Ideas" but not cupcakes. The list holds 50 entries of up to 40 characters, starts empty, and goes into settings files with your switches. Boards named after a muted word stay.
- New Keep Home feed patch, with its switch on the Feed page. Pinterest reloads Home with new pins on its own when you come back after five minutes or more, when you pick the Home tab again after a while and when you back out of a search, and the pin you were about to open is gone. With this on, Home stays where you left it. Pull down whenever you want new pins. The new pins prompt, a second tap on the Home tab and a pin you open from a notification still load as before. It starts off.
- New Show posted date patch, with its switch on the Interface page. Pinterest sends the day each pin was posted but never shows it, and with this on you see "Posted" and that day under the title when you open a pin. A pin without a date just doesn't get the line. The date follows the language HushPinterest shows and your phone's time zone. It starts off and shows from the next pin you open. (#11)
- With Debug logging on, the line for a kept pin also says whether Pinterest marked it as a repin or as saved to one of your boards. It shows only that the field is set, never which board.
- The Feed page has a new row under the AI switches, Pinterest's own AI setting. It opens the page where Pinterest lets you see fewer AI pins among the ones it picks for you, since neither that page nor the switches catch every AI pin alone. It's there whenever Hide AI-labeled pins is patched in.

## Behind the scenes

- The pin model fixture test also checks the fields Hide video pins reads, the two inside Pinterest's video and idea pin models included, and the grid title that the AI words and video filters use to tell a pin from other models.
- The pre-push and release checks take a declared build kept as APKMirror's `.apkm` bundle, since that's the only way 14.41.0 ships. The bug report form's example names a bundle too, and the release step keeps whatever kind of file the form names.
- The release gate's advisory check works in Windows PowerShell 5.1 again. Since 0.0.11, any failed OSV request stopped it there with an "Unable to find type" error. A dropped connection or a busy server now gets asked again in 5.1, the way it already did in PowerShell 7.
- The README's Help now goes through why Android might refuse the install. It says where Manager keeps its signing key, so an update that won't go over your patched copy can be fixed without losing your settings. It also covers stock Pinterest and the unknown apps prompt.
- The README sends people on v0.0.11 to Pinterest 14.40.0 again, the build that release patches, and names 14.41.0 as the next release's build. It had pointed them at 14.41.0, which v0.0.11 refuses. The release's prepare step now stops while the README still names a next release, so it gets rewritten for the new build before a release is cut.
- The patch verifier checks how the long-press hide switches tell Pinterest's buttons apart. The sorter has to read the held button's own id and send Save, Send and both search ids to the right answer, with the ids found the way the patch finds them, and a build without them has to keep the plain answer.
- The bug report form lists Filter feed among the patches you can tick. It was the one patch the form left out, and the release check stopped on that.
- The release check and the publish step leave a GitHub description alone when it names no version, patch count or Pinterest build, since there's nothing in it to go stale. One that names any of them still has to match the release. This release would have stopped on the shorter description the repository uses now.
- The source census reads Jman's bundle registry again. On October 14 the registry took down the files the audit read and now serves the same list from its own site, so every audit since stopped on a missing file. It reads all of the site's pages, not only the first hundred releases.
- The device scripts write their lease times in UTC with a `Z` at the end. They used `+00:00`, and the other tools sharing the test phone took a lease written that way as already expired. They also read a `Z` time as UTC now. Before, a busy phone's expiry was read as local clock time, so an expired lease looked hours from ending.
- The script tests now clean up after themselves. The pre-push cases remove the worktree the hook builds in, and a passing host reference run deletes its report folder. Each run used to leave both in the temp directory.

## Install

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 1.34.0 or newer.
2. Add HushPinterest as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushPinterest
3. Download Pinterest 14.41.0, version code `14418010`. APKMirror has it as an arm64-v8a bundle (`.apkm`) for Android 12L or newer. Pick that file in Manager and it merges the parts before patching.
4. Uninstall the stock Pinterest first, since Android won't put one over the other. Save anything you keep only on the phone before you do. Your boards and pins come back when you sign in.
5. Sign in with your email and a Pinterest password. If you joined through Google or Facebook, tap `Forgot your password?` on Pinterest's login page to set one first.
6. Right after your first patch, export Morphe Manager's signing key (Settings, then System, then Import & export, then Signing key) and keep it somewhere private. Updates only install over a Pinterest signed with that same key.

Already on HushPinterest? Skip steps 4 and 5. Patch 14.41.0 with the same key and install it over the one you have.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Pinterest APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushPinterest#install). `SHA256SUMS.txt` is signed with the HushPinterest release key, fingerprint `FCE5 ECE3 182A 647B 3AF2  C5ED 2DC3 5E8D 5C00 E8A6`. [How to check a download](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushPinterest#verify-a-release-download).

## Reported issues

- #2: Download pin now shows in the full-screen pin menu some accounts get from a pin's three dots, so it's there whichever menu Pinterest gives you.
- #11: Copy image and Share image under Download pin, the three long-press hide switches and Show posted date all came from this one.
- #12: Black comments covers the gray strip under the status bar now, on photo and video pins.
- #13: There's a new switch, Hide Search image label on pins, that takes the label off the lens button.
- #14: Hide suggested replies takes away the row of ready-made replies next to the comment box.

## Validation

All 232 patch tests and 1067 extension tests passed on this commit, none skipped. The bundle attached here was patched onto a real Pinterest 14.41.0 bundle from APKMirror with Morphe's desktop patcher, and all 32 patches applied without forcing. `release-receipt-0.0.12.json` records that result, the bundle's hash and what patching changed in the app's manifest.

Before release, these patches went on a signed-in phone running Pinterest 14.41.0, installed over 0.0.11 with the same key, so the sign-in and settings carried over. The new switches were tried there one at a time: Filter feed, Keep Home feed, Show posted date, Copy and Share image, the long-press hides, Hide suggested replies, Hide pins that say they're AI and the full-screen menu's Download rows. repos.title: v0.0.12
repos.body:
HushPinterest 0.0.12 has 32 patches for Pinterest 14.41.0. It's built on Morphe patcher 1.15.1, so it needs Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer. This one moves to Pinterest's newest version and adds a lot of new switches, every one of them off until you turn it on. Filter feed can hide video pins and pins with words you mute. Keep Home feed stops Home from reloading on its own when you come back to it, and Show posted date puts the day a pin went up under its title. Download pins can copy or share the picture itself now, and its rows show in the full-screen pin menu too. Downloads also stopped settling for the smaller copy now and then.

It's a new Pinterest version. So far APKMirror only has 14.41.0 as an arm64 bundle (`.apkm`) for Android 12L or newer, and Manager merges it before patching. Patch it with the same signing key you used before and install it over your current HushPinterest, and your settings stay as they are. On a phone older than Android 12L, keep 0.0.11 and Pinterest 14.40.0 for now.

## What's new

- The patches now target Pinterest 14.41.0, the newest stable release. 14.40.0 is no longer supported. So far APKMirror has 14.41.0 only as an arm64 bundle (`.apkm`) for Android 12L or newer, and Manager merges it before patching.
- Download pin now shows in the full-screen pin menu some accounts get from the three dots on a pin, along with the other Hush rows, and Pinterest's own Download row in that menu gives way to it. Before, only the smaller pop-up menu had them.
- Download pins has a new switch, Copy image, that starts off. It adds a Copy image row under Download pin, in the small pin menu and in the full-screen one, and puts the full-size picture on the clipboard so you can paste it into a chat or a notes app. Video pins don't get the row. If the picture is too big, isn't really an image, or takes too long, you're told so and your clipboard stays as it was. (#11)
- Download pins also has Share image, another switch that starts off. Its row sits under Copy image and opens Android's share menu with the full-size picture itself rather than a link, so the app you pick gets the image. Video pins don't get it, and if the picture can't be fetched you get a short note instead of the share menu. (#11)
- Long-press download has three new switches on the Pin actions page: Hide Save, Hide Send and Hide Search image in the long-press menu. Each takes that one Pinterest button out of the round menu you get by holding a pin in a grid, and the pin itself still saves, shares and searches as before. They work with Download off too. If everything would be hidden and Download is off, the menu stays Pinterest's own rather than opening empty. All three start off. (#11)
- Black comments now covers the strip under the status bar too. On 14.41.0 the comments fill the whole screen, and that strip stayed dark gray above the black list on photo and video pins alike.
- Downloads no longer save the smaller copy now and then when the original is there. Finding the original asks Pinterest's media server a few quick questions, and one asked just as both lookup helpers were wrapping up the last was turned away, so the download settled for the size the feed showed. It now waits a moment for a helper to come free.
- Copy media link no longer overwrites something you copied after it. When a pin shows only a smaller size, the link to that size goes on the clipboard right away, and it becomes the original's link once Pinterest's media server answers, but only if the clipboard still holds that copy. Before, nothing was copied until the answer came, and a slow answer could replace whatever you'd copied in the meantime.
- Save list no longer hangs when the app holding the picked file stops answering. Each save gets 30 seconds in all, then you're told to check the file, and a late answer from that app doesn't add another message or remove anything. While that app is still busy, a new list says to try later instead of opening a picker. Everything that talks to the file's app now runs on its own helper, never on the screen's thread, including the clean-up after a list that couldn't be written while HushPinterest was paused.
- A list that isn't written no longer deletes an empty file you picked to write over. Only an empty file made since the picker opened gets removed. Any other file is left where it is, and you're told so.
- Save list leaves out a source link that hides a session code behind an encoded `;` (`%3B`, that encoded again, or a longer spelling some servers still read as `;`), the way it already left out a plain `;jsessionid=`. The pin's ID, title and Pinterest link still go in. Ordinary encoded spaces and accented letters stay exactly as given.
- Queue selected and Queue pins stay off until something chosen can actually be saved. A pin with no picture address, or a video Pinterest only streams, doesn't turn them on anymore, though Save list still takes those pins. A mix still queues what it can and counts the rest as unsupported.
- Morphe Manager lists every change of the release your Pinterest was patched with, not just a short summary. For that one release Manager shows the patch bundle's description instead of this changelog, and the description was one paragraph while every older release listed its changes. It now goes on with the release's changes after the summary, starting with this one.
- Hide comments has a second switch, Hide suggested replies, for the row of ready-made replies like "Yum!" and "Came out great!" next to the comment box. You can still write your own comment. It starts off, and the two switches don't turn each other on. (#14)
- Hide AI-labeled pins has a second switch, Hide pins that say they're AI, for AI pins Pinterest doesn't label. It takes a pin whose title or description says something like "AI art", "AI generated", #aiart, "made with AI", Midjourney, Stable Diffusion or PixAI, and pins from sites that only host AI images, like pixai.art and Civitai. It goes by the pin's own words, so a pin that just says "AI" stays, and names like Ai Weiwei or the Portuguese "aí" are left alone. Boards named that way stay too. It starts off, and diagnostics count these pins apart from the labeled ones.
- Hide closeup buttons has a third switch, Hide Search image label on pins. Pinterest puts a "Search image" label on the lens button for your first two pins each day, and with this on the lens shows without it, the way it looks from the third pin on. Tapping the lens still searches. It starts off and sits under Hide lens button on the Interface page. (#13)
- New Filter feed patch, with a Hide video pins switch on the Feed page. It takes pins that play a video out of your home feed, search, related pins and boards, idea pins with video included. Photos and GIFs stay. It starts off.
- Filter feed also has Muted words, a row on the Feed page where you type words and phrases you don't want to see. A pin whose title or description has one of them leaves the same lists. Capitals don't matter and only whole words count, so "cake" takes out "Wedding Cake Ideas" but not cupcakes. The list holds 50 entries of up to 40 characters, starts empty, and goes into settings files with your switches. Boards named after a muted word stay.
- New Keep Home feed patch, with its switch on the Feed page. Pinterest reloads Home with new pins on its own when you come back after five minutes or more, when you pick the Home tab again after a while and when you back out of a search, and the pin you were about to open is gone. With this on, Home stays where you left it. Pull down whenever you want new pins. The new pins prompt, a second tap on the Home tab and a pin you open from a notification still load as before. It starts off.
- New Show posted date patch, with its switch on the Interface page. Pinterest sends the day each pin was posted but never shows it, and with this on you see "Posted" and that day under the title when you open a pin. A pin without a date just doesn't get the line. The date follows the language HushPinterest shows and your phone's time zone. It starts off and shows from the next pin you open. (#11)
- With Debug logging on, the line for a kept pin also says whether Pinterest marked it as a repin or as saved to one of your boards. It shows only that the field is set, never which board.
- The Feed page has a new row under the AI switches, Pinterest's own AI setting. It opens the page where Pinterest lets you see fewer AI pins among the ones it picks for you, since neither that page nor the switches catch every AI pin alone. It's there whenever Hide AI-labeled pins is patched in.

## Behind the scenes

- The pin model fixture test also checks the fields Hide video pins reads, the two inside Pinterest's video and idea pin models included, and the grid title that the AI words and video filters use to tell a pin from other models.
- The pre-push and release checks take a declared build kept as APKMirror's `.apkm` bundle, since that's the only way 14.41.0 ships. The bug report form's example names a bundle too, and the release step keeps whatever kind of file the form names.
- The release gate's advisory check works in Windows PowerShell 5.1 again. Since 0.0.11, any failed OSV request stopped it there with an "Unable to find type" error. A dropped connection or a busy server now gets asked again in 5.1, the way it already did in PowerShell 7.
- The README's Help now goes through why Android might refuse the install. It says where Manager keeps its signing key, so an update that won't go over your patched copy can be fixed without losing your settings. It also covers stock Pinterest and the unknown apps prompt.
- The README sends people on v0.0.11 to Pinterest 14.40.0 again, the build that release patches, and names 14.41.0 as the next release's build. It had pointed them at 14.41.0, which v0.0.11 refuses. The release's prepare step now stops while the README still names a next release, so it gets rewritten for the new build before a release is cut.
- The patch verifier checks how the long-press hide switches tell Pinterest's buttons apart. The sorter has to read the held button's own id and send Save, Send and both search ids to the right answer, with the ids found the way the patch finds them, and a build without them has to keep the plain answer.
- The bug report form lists Filter feed among the patches you can tick. It was the one patch the form left out, and the release check stopped on that.
- The release check and the publish step leave a GitHub description alone when it names no version, patch count or Pinterest build, since there's nothing in it to go stale. One that names any of them still has to match the release. This release would have stopped on the shorter description the repository uses now.
- The source census reads Jman's bundle registry again. On October 14 the registry took down the files the audit read and now serves the same list from its own site, so every audit since stopped on a missing file. It reads all of the site's pages, not only the first hundred releases.
- The device scripts write their lease times in UTC with a `Z` at the end. They used `+00:00`, and the other tools sharing the test phone took a lease written that way as already expired. They also read a `Z` time as UTC now. Before, a busy phone's expiry was read as local clock time, so an expired lease looked hours from ending.
- The script tests now clean up after themselves. The pre-push cases remove the worktree the hook builds in, and a passing host reference run deletes its report folder. Each run used to leave both in the temp directory.

## Install

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 1.34.0 or newer.
2. Add HushPinterest as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushPinterest
3. Download Pinterest 14.41.0, version code `14418010`. APKMirror has it as an arm64-v8a bundle (`.apkm`) for Android 12L or newer. Pick that file in Manager and it merges the parts before patching.
4. Uninstall the stock Pinterest first, since Android won't put one over the other. Save anything you keep only on the phone before you do. Your boards and pins come back when you sign in.
5. Sign in with your email and a Pinterest password. If you joined through Google or Facebook, tap `Forgot your password?` on Pinterest's login page to set one first.
6. Right after your first patch, export Morphe Manager's signing key (Settings, then System, then Import & export, then Signing key) and keep it somewhere private. Updates only install over a Pinterest signed with that same key.

Already on HushPinterest? Skip steps 4 and 5. Patch 14.41.0 with the same key and install it over the one you have.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Pinterest APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushPinterest#install). `SHA256SUMS.txt` is signed with the HushPinterest release key, fingerprint `FCE5 ECE3 182A 647B 3AF2  C5ED 2DC3 5E8D 5C00 E8A6`. [How to check a download](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushPinterest#verify-a-release-download).

## Reported issues

- #2: Download pin now shows in the full-screen pin menu some accounts get from a pin's three dots, so it's there whichever menu Pinterest gives you.
- #11: Copy image and Share image under Download pin, the three long-press hide switches and Show posted date all came from this one.
- #12: Black comments covers the gray strip under the status bar now, on photo and video pins.
- #13: There's a new switch, Hide Search image label on pins, that takes the label off the lens button.
- #14: Hide suggested replies takes away the row of ready-made replies next to the comment box.

## Validation

All 232 patch tests and 1067 extension tests passed on this commit, none skipped. The bundle attached here was patched onto a real Pinterest 14.41.0 bundle from APKMirror with Morphe's desktop patcher, and all 32 patches applied without forcing. `release-receipt-0.0.12.json` records that result, the bundle's hash and what patching changed in the app's manifest.

Before release, these patches went on a signed-in phone running Pinterest 14.41.0, installed over 0.0.11 with the same key, so the sign-in and settings carried over. The new switches were tried there one at a time: Filter feed, Keep Home feed, Show posted date, Copy and Share image, the long-press hides, Hide suggested replies, Hide pins that say they're AI and the full-screen menu's Download rows. Black comments left no gray strip under the status bar, and Black bottom bar and Black pin menu stayed black on the new version. Copy media link put the smaller size's link on the clipboard right away and swapped in the original's once Pinterest answered. Queue selected stayed off until a pin was picked, Save list wrote its file, and the Feed page's new row opened Pinterest's own AI setting.

The Search image label switch is covered by tests but wasn't seen on the phone, since Pinterest only shows that label on the first two pins each day. Copy media link leaving a newer copy alone and Save list's 30 second limit are covered by tests too.

hushtelegram.title: v0.0.19
hushtelegram.body:
HushTelegram v0.0.19 has 67 patches for Telegram 13.0.3, and it patches two builds now. One is telegram.org's (`org.telegram.messenger.web`, version code 71839). The other is the build from Google Play (`org.telegram.messenger`, version code 71831), the one most people already have on their phone. Sixty-three are selected by default, and every new switch starts off. The last release only knew telegram.org's build, so Morphe Manager turned the Play APK away with "Wrong package selected." Now either one patches, and telegram.org's build works exactly as it did. The official beta isn't a target anymore. If you're on it, move to telegram.org's build or the Play one before you patch. The first time you sign in, Telegram may turn down the API ID that ships with any patched build and show `API_ID_PUBLISHED_FLOOD`, so no login code arrives. It's the same on every patched Telegram, HushTelegram included. The one-time fix is to register your own Telegram API credentials, and the steps are under Install.

## What's new

* **Telegram:** The Google Play version of Telegram 13.0.3 (`org.telegram.messenger`, version code 71831) can be patched now. That's the APK APKMirror and Uptodown carry, and Morphe Manager used to turn it away with "Wrong package selected" because it only knew telegram.org's build. telegram.org's build still works the same way.
* **Telegram:** **Repair Firebase push registration** also covers the Play build, so its notifications sign up with Google like they do on telegram.org's build.
* **Telegram:** The official Telegram beta isn't a target anymore. **Turn off beta debug logs** is gone with it, and so is the part of **Disable analytics** that only stopped the beta's crash and session reports. If you're on the beta, switch to telegram.org's build or the Play build before you patch.

### Tooling

* **Tooling:** The release's clean-APK check accepts the Google Play build as a vendor baseline. It now asks that the signing certificate the catalog declares for the package be present on the APK, and it allows the extra certificate Google Play App Signing adds. Before, it required every certificate on the APK to be one the catalog declared, so the Play build's Google certificate stopped the release even though the patcher applied every patch to it.

## Install

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 1.34.0 or newer.
2. Add HushTelegram as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushTelegram
3. Get Telegram 13.0.3. Two builds work: telegram.org's [Download button](https://telegram.org/android) (`org.telegram.messenger.web`, version code 71839) and the Google Play build (`org.telegram.messenger`, version code 71831), the one most people already have, which [APKMirror](https://www.apkmirror.com/apk/telegram-fz-llc/telegram/) and Uptodown also carry. The patched app needs Android 9 or newer.
4. Coming from an earlier HushTelegram on telegram.org's build? Patch the new 13.0.3 APK and install it over your current HushTelegram with the same Morphe Manager signing key. On the beta? It isn't a target now, so switch to telegram.org's build or the Play build, patch that, and install it fresh, since it's a different app than the beta and Android won't put one over the other. New to HushTelegram? Uninstall the stock Telegram first, for the same reason. Your chats come back when you sign in, but secret chats don't. Back up Morphe Manager's signing key after your first patch. You'll need it for every update.
5. If Telegram turns down your login code with `API_ID_PUBLISHED_FLOOD`, that's Telegram refusing the public API ID that ships with any patched build, the Play one included. Register your own app at [my.telegram.org/apps](https://my.telegram.org/apps), using only letters and numbers in the short name. Then select `Use registered Telegram API credentials`, fill in `apiId` and `apiHash`, and patch again. The result installs over your current HushTelegram build. Keep both values private.
6. Want HushTelegram's own icon, or Telegram's logo in white on the black launch screen? Turn on Expert mode in Morphe Manager and pick `HushTelegram icon and name` or `Black and white launch logo` before you patch.
7. For notifications, open Telegram's Settings, tap Notifications, and turn on `Keep-Alive Service` and `Background Connection` under Other, near the bottom of the page. Phones where Firebase notifications don't come through can also try the `UnifiedPush notifications` switch on HushTelegram's Notifications page with a UnifiedPush app like ntfy.
8. To change HushTelegram's switches, open Telegram's Settings and tap HushTelegram settings, or press and hold the Telegram title at the top of your chat list. The side menu is the `Side menu` switch on the Chat list page.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Telegram APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushTelegram#install).

## Validation

All 1348 runtime tests passed locally, and all 481 patch tests passed too, along with both Android lints (the shared library and the Telegram extension). Every one of the 67 patches applied to Telegram 13.0.3 without forcing, on both telegram.org's build (version code 71839) and the Google Play build (version code 71831). For each patched build the release receipt checked the package name, version, manifest, native libraries and zip alignment. The Google Play build was also installed on a clean Android 13 system and launched straight to Telegram's sign-in screen with no crash.

repos.title: v0.0.19
repos.body:
HushTelegram v0.0.19 has 67 patches for Telegram 13.0.3, and it patches two builds now. One is telegram.org's (`org.telegram.messenger.web`, version code 71839). The other is the build from Google Play (`org.telegram.messenger`, version code 71831), the one most people already have on their phone. Sixty-three are selected by default, and every new switch starts off. The last release only knew telegram.org's build, so Morphe Manager turned the Play APK away with "Wrong package selected." Now either one patches, and telegram.org's build works exactly as it did. The official beta isn't a target anymore. If you're on it, move to telegram.org's build or the Play one before you patch. The first time you sign in, Telegram may turn down the API ID that ships with any patched build and show `API_ID_PUBLISHED_FLOOD`, so no login code arrives. It's the same on every patched Telegram, HushTelegram included. The one-time fix is to register your own Telegram API credentials, and the steps are under Install.

## What's new

* **Telegram:** The Google Play version of Telegram 13.0.3 (`org.telegram.messenger`, version code 71831) can be patched now. That's the APK APKMirror and Uptodown carry, and Morphe Manager used to turn it away with "Wrong package selected" because it only knew telegram.org's build. telegram.org's build still works the same way.
* **Telegram:** **Repair Firebase push registration** also covers the Play build, so its notifications sign up with Google like they do on telegram.org's build.
* **Telegram:** The official Telegram beta isn't a target anymore. **Turn off beta debug logs** is gone with it, and so is the part of **Disable analytics** that only stopped the beta's crash and session reports. If you're on the beta, switch to telegram.org's build or the Play build before you patch.

### Tooling

* **Tooling:** The release's clean-APK check accepts the Google Play build as a vendor baseline. It now asks that the signing certificate the catalog declares for the package be present on the APK, and it allows the extra certificate Google Play App Signing adds. Before, it required every certificate on the APK to be one the catalog declared, so the Play build's Google certificate stopped the release even though the patcher applied every patch to it.

## Install

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 1.34.0 or newer.
2. Add HushTelegram as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushTelegram
3. Get Telegram 13.0.3. Two builds work: telegram.org's [Download button](https://telegram.org/android) (`org.telegram.messenger.web`, version code 71839) and the Google Play build (`org.telegram.messenger`, version code 71831), the one most people already have, which [APKMirror](https://www.apkmirror.com/apk/telegram-fz-llc/telegram/) and Uptodown also carry. The patched app needs Android 9 or newer.
4. Coming from an earlier HushTelegram on telegram.org's build? Patch the new 13.0.3 APK and install it over your current HushTelegram with the same Morphe Manager signing key. On the beta? It isn't a target now, so switch to telegram.org's build or the Play build, patch that, and install it fresh, since it's a different app than the beta and Android won't put one over the other. New to HushTelegram? Uninstall the stock Telegram first, for the same reason. Your chats come back when you sign in, but secret chats don't. Back up Morphe Manager's signing key after your first patch. You'll need it for every update.
5. If Telegram turns down your login code with `API_ID_PUBLISHED_FLOOD`, that's Telegram refusing the public API ID that ships with any patched build, the Play one included. Register your own app at [my.telegram.org/apps](https://my.telegram.org/apps), using only letters and numbers in the short name. Then select `Use registered Telegram API credentials`, fill in `apiId` and `apiHash`, and patch again. The result installs over your current HushTelegram build. Keep both values private.
6. Want HushTelegram's own icon, or Telegram's logo in white on the black launch screen? Turn on Expert mode in Morphe Manager and pick `HushTelegram icon and name` or `Black and white launch logo` before you patch.
7. For notifications, open Telegram's Settings, tap Notifications, and turn on `Keep-Alive Service` and `Background Connection` under Other, near the bottom of the page. Phones where Firebase notifications don't come through can also try the `UnifiedPush notifications` switch on HushTelegram's Notifications page with a UnifiedPush app like ntfy.
8. To change HushTelegram's switches, open Telegram's Settings and tap HushTelegram settings, or press and hold the Telegram title at the top of your chat list. The side menu is the `Side menu` switch on the Chat list page.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Telegram APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushTelegram#install).

## Validation

All 1348 runtime tests passed locally, and all 481 patch tests passed too, along with both Android lints (the shared library and the Telegram extension). Every one of the 67 patches applied to Telegram 13.0.3 without forcing, on both telegram.org's build (version code 71839) and the Google Play build (version code 71831). For each patched build the release receipt checked the package name, version, manifest, native libraries and zip alignment. The Google Play build was also installed on a clean Android 13 system and launched straight to Telegram's sign-in screen with no crash.

hushthreads.title: v0.0.15
hushthreads.body:
HushThreads v0.0.15 has 19 patches for Threads 451.0.0.51.80 (`com.instagram.barcelona`), and it patches that version only. It's built on Morphe patcher 1.15.1, so you need Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer.

Copy text is back on opened posts, and Open links in browser now catches ad links and lead form links too. Settings got Quick setups for changing several switches in one tap, a Report a problem row that fills in your versions for you, and they stay open now when Threads redraws itself. Saving photos and videos got a lot of fixes, the biggest one for phones with smaller screens, where Save photo saved nothing.

**Your reports in this release**

- [#9](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/9) found that Copy text didn't do anything on an opened post. Pressing and holding the post's text brings up Copy text again, and the new `Copy text on long press` switch under Posts turns it on or off.
- [HushFacebook#146](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushFacebook/issues/146) asked for a way to keep HushThreads settings out of the menu you get by holding Threads' icon. The new `Settings shortcut on the app icon` switch on the Pause, backup and diagnostics page does that, and the Threads logo still opens settings with a long press.

## Threads

- Don't want HushThreads settings in the menu you get by holding Threads' icon? Turn off the new `Settings shortcut on the app icon` switch on the Pause, backup and diagnostics page and it leaves that menu right away, while Threads' own shortcuts stay. A long press on the Threads logo and the HushThreads row in Threads' settings still open the settings, and Pause leaves the switch as you set it.
- Pressing and holding the text of an opened post brings up Copy text again, the same as in your feed, so you get the whole post with its links. It had stopped doing anything on 451. A new `Copy text on long press` switch under Posts in HushThreads settings turns this on or off. It starts on and comes with every build.
- Open links in browser now also covers the places on 451 that used to skip it. An ad's link button and a swipe up on an ad in the media viewer send the ad's web link to your browser the same way post links go, and so do the privacy policy and disclaimer links on a lead form. Meta's own pages still open in Threads.
- Search's Follow suggestions row is gone too. It has its own switch, `Hide follow suggestions in Search`, right under Hide suggested users on the Feed page, and it starts on. Nothing takes the row's place, and search results and topics stay as they are. Turn the switch off, or pause HushThreads, and Search looks the way Threads draws it.
- Save photo and Save all work on phones with smaller screens again. On a 720 px wide screen Threads only keeps a photo at up to 750 px, and HushThreads took every one of those for a thumbnail and saved nothing. It now saves the largest copy there is, still prefers a full size one when Threads has it, and still never saves an avatar-sized copy.
- Disable video autoplay now also tells Threads' video prefetcher to hold off. The switch only held a feed video at its cover frame, so Threads could still start downloading a held video ahead of time. The patch now answers the prefetcher's autoplay-off question itself, only where the prefetcher asks it, so Instagram's older autoplay checker is left alone. With the switch off, paused or in safe mode, Threads' own answer goes back as before. Checked on a Galaxy S22 with Threads 451. The prefetcher got the hold answer with the switch on and Threads' own with it off, and a tapped video still played full screen.
- The HushThreads settings home page has two new rows. `Quick setups` changes a set of switches in one tap: Quiet hides ads and suggested accounts, Privacy stops most usage reports, takes tracking off shared links and hides your screenshots from Threads, and Back to defaults puts every feature switch back. A toast says how many changed. `Report a problem` opens a new GitHub bug report with your HushThreads and Threads versions, your phone and the switches you have on already filled in.
- More settings is now a heading on the HushThreads settings home page, with Appearance, Links, Updates, Set when you patched, Pause, backup and diagnostics and About listed under it. Every page is one tap from home and Back always goes home. Report a problem and Support HushThreads are still the last two rows, and the patch descriptions and bug report form point to the shorter paths.
- Don't use Quick setups? Press and hold its row on the settings home page and it's gone, and its help line says so. To bring it back, tap the Quick setups row on the Pause, backup and diagnostics page. Screen readers get the same press and hold on that row, and no other row offers one.
- HushThreads settings stay open when Threads redraws itself, after you change the font size or switch dark theme from the quick settings, or when Android closes Threads in the background and you come back. They used to close. They now come back on the page you were on. That holds with the settings open over two Threads screens and one of them closed, and on Android 9 in split screen when the Threads side sits for more than 30 seconds before you tap back into it.
- A settings file you pick for Import or Export isn't lost anymore when Threads redraws itself while the file picker is open, after a font size or dark theme change, or when Android closes Threads in the background to make room. The settings came back as if you hadn't picked anything. The file picker now opens through a small invisible screen of HushThreads' own, which keeps your pick until the settings are back. Access to the file ends once it's read or written. If Android closes Threads before that, it ends the next time Threads starts. Two quick taps on Import or Export open one picker, not two.
- After an export or import, the Export settings or Import settings row says how it went, in full, until you run another. That message used to show only in a pop-up, and newer Android versions cut those off after two lines, so a refusal like a damaged file lost its "Nothing was changed."
- Save's messages are short enough to read whole on Android 12 and later, which cut a message after two lines. On an S22 the proxy message stopped mid-word, and the slow-download one was just as long. A carousel's result now shows each line as its own message, so a line under the counts, like a proxy asking for a password, isn't lost. The German, Spanish, Indonesian, Portuguese and Turkish wording was shortened to fit too.
- A download that only trickles in now stops after ten minutes per file and says it was too slow, instead of holding one of the three save slots for as long as the server likes. A host lookup that never answers gives up after 20 seconds, and Cancel now ends a save that's still waiting on one.
- Cancel and the download time limit now end a save even when the phone's proxy service stops answering. Waiting proxy calls share the fixed limit on background network checks, so repeated attempts can't keep creating threads.
- A save's download now has a connection of its own that never asks Threads' cookie store or sign-in prompts for anything, so it can't send a cookie or a password, and it drops every cookie a server or a redirect sets. It still goes through the proxy your Wi-Fi or phone settings name and checks the server's certificate the same way. If that proxy asks for a password, the save stops and tells you, since it never sends one.
- On Android 9, a save without Threads' Storage permission now stops before it downloads anything and tells you where to turn the permission on. A carousel stops fetching its remaining pages if the permission is taken away partway through.
- Joining the picture and sound of a VP9 save (or AV1 before Android 14) now stops before it would take more than 24 MB of memory, and the save falls back to the single file. A file built from millions of tiny parts can't run Threads out of memory that way anymore. Cancel is also noticed while the join is still reading the tracks.
- When a save finds no picture or video it can keep, the diagnostics report now lists the kind and size of every address it looked at, so a bug report shows why. It never includes the addresses themselves.
- When the regular Instagram app from Meta sits beside your patched Threads, the Links page in HushThreads settings says Instagram won't open Threads posts or profiles here. That's Instagram's own check, and it's why Instagram says it couldn't load the website.
- When the settings list can't be put on the HushThreads screen at all, the screen shows Retry and Back instead of staying blank. Retry opens the page you were headed to, with your switches as you left them.
- When Threads rebuilds its screen with the settings open (after a text size change, say, or when Android closed Threads in the background), a settings page that fails to come back now gives way to a fresh page. - When the final APK check catches the direct browser hook overwriting something Threads still needs, it now says which case it found. Every override check in the post row has to carry the patch's hook, which hands the override and its own action to the extension in a free local and casts the answer back, and PostText has to ask about its selection switch first thing. Each hash is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the file's raw bytes.

It follows the list's own total across short pages within a request and row budget, reads renamed repositories under their current names, and counts a repository as a Threads bundle only for a current release with verified metadata. 2. Patch the arm64-v8a bundle of Threads 451.0.0.51.80 (version code 512108444), the same Threads build as v0.0.14.

That happens when a build doesn't evaluate every project, as under configure-on-demand, and the refusal names each one. Its Guava probe also stopped failing every Gradle command when it can't find one of the two plugins. It records no jar for that plugin now, and only the inventory refuses. A refused run also deletes the previous inventory, so nothing reads an old one as this run's.
- The same classpath now resolves commons-lang3 3.18.0 instead of the 3.16.0 the Morphe plugin asks for, which is inside GHSA-j288-q9x7-2f5v (CVE-2025-48924, 3.0 to 3.17.0). That was the last advisory OSV reported for the build's 114 plugin components, and the build advisory gate now finds none. It's a floor too, so it goes quiet once the plugin asks for 3.18.0 or later.
- The classpath the build plugins run from now resolves Guava 33.7.2-jre instead of 33.5.0-jre, which is inside GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94 (CVE-2026-102554, 4.0 to 33.7.1). It's a floor, so a plugin that later asks for a newer Guava still gets it. The build classpath inventory also records which jar the Morphe and Android Gradle plugins really load the advisory's three classes from, and it refuses to write when that isn't the Guava the classpath resolved. The bundle build and the focused registry tests pass with it.
- The source census now waits out a rate limit for as long as the answer says. GitLab throttles unauthenticated reads and answers 429 with the time its limit resets, and the census used to wait a flat 61 seconds, so a long reset used up its three tries and failed the run. It waits until the reset that Retry-After (seconds or a date), RateLimit-Reset or X-RateLimit-Reset names, plus a second, capped at 15 minutes by `-MaxRateLimitWaitSeconds`. An answer that names no reset still waits `-RateLimitWaitSeconds`, and a fourth limit in a row still fails the source. The run log also says whether GitLab was read with a token, since a token raises the limit.
- The source census reads the Morphe Patch Tracker again. Its list now carries a couple of bundles twice under keys that differ only in case (immortalzeus:dev and ImmortalZeus:dev), and the census refused the whole file as unreadable JSON. It reads those keys as they are now and counts each repository once, in PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1 alike.
- The final APK check now holds Hide suggested users on profiles to its own contract. It finds both places from the clean DEX alone: the profile screen's suggested accounts carousel, which has to hand its list to the extension right before Threads' own null check and cast the answer back, and the header row, which has to ask first thing on its path and leave by its check's other side through a local nothing reads. A build without the patch has to leave both as Threads wrote them, with no call to the extension anywhere.
- The final APK check now holds Copy text on long press to its own contract whenever Settings is selected. Every override check in the post row has to carry the patch's hook, which hands the override and its own action to the extension in a free local and casts the answer back, and PostText has to ask about its selection switch first thing. A build without Settings has to leave both exactly as Threads wrote them.
- The build classpath inventory now records a SHA-256 of settings.gradle.kts, patches/build.gradle.kts, gradle/libs.versions.toml and gradle/verification-metadata.xml, and the release receipt refuses an inventory whose hash for any of them differs from the checkout, naming the file. Before, only the settings script was checked, so a changed plugin version or dependency pin could leave an old inventory standing for the new build. Each hash is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the file's raw bytes.
- The source census reads Jman's Patch Bundle Registry now, through its registration file and the paged Threads list, because the old bundle files there answer 404. It follows the list's own total across short pages within a request and row budget, reads renamed repositories under their current names, and counts a repository as a Threads bundle only for a current release with verified metadata. History, unverified entries and a bare registration are reported but not promoted, and a list it can't finish reading fails the census. The source ledger points its Jman entry at the registry too, with HushThreads' registration there as the listing's evidence.
- Updated the build wrapper to Gradle 9.8.1, which fixes three high security advisories. The build advisory check now checks the recorded Gradle distribution separately from component libraries and refuses missing or unreadable version evidence, including when online component checks are skipped.
- A fixture test checks on 451 that both of the post row's long press override checks and PostText's selection flag go through the extension, and that a jump straight to an override check or a selection flag written over before PostText copies it stops the patch.
- The release receipt now asks OSV about the plugin classpath that builds and signs the bundle too, from an inventory settings.gradle.kts writes after each bundle build, and reports it apart from what the bundle carries, with its own exception list. A version that was only asked for and resolved to another is listed as a request, and a missing inventory or a dependency that didn't resolve stops the release instead of reading as clean.
- The bundle build holds the Android Gradle plugin's jose4j at 0.9.6 and jdom2 at 2.0.6.1, the patch releases that fix their high advisories, so the plugin classpath has none left.

## Update

1. You need [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 1.34.0 or newer. If HushThreads is already one of your patch sources, Manager shows 0.0.15 once it refreshes. If it isn't, add it: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushThreads
2. Patch the arm64-v8a bundle of Threads 451.0.0.51.80 (version code 512108444), the same Threads build as v0.0.14.
3. Manager's default selection has every patch except `Change version code`, `Remove share targets` and `Trust user-added certificates`. Turn on Expert mode if you want any of those.
4. Patch with the Morphe Manager signing key you used last time. That's what lets the update install over your patched Threads and keep your data and your login. Coming from the stock Threads, uninstall it first.
5. On a fresh install, sign in with your Instagram username and password.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Threads APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads#install).

## Validation

994 runtime tests and 281 patch tests passed locally, along with both Android lints and the release script checks. All 19 patches applied without forcing to Threads 451.0.0.51.80, and the release receipt records the run. The dependency advisory check passed.
